page.layout: One page of text: running head centred at top, with the page number at the top left. Below it a title in two lines, then a woodcut engraving in the centre. Below the engraving a four-line verse, centred. At the bottom right a catchword.

l.i: Quisquis es in speculo tanquam tua discute facta:
Et quid te deceat, dispice, quidue minus;
Censorem alterius nunquam tu te oggere labis,
Quin prius explores singula quæq; tua.

page.notes: The engraving shows a cockerel perched on an hourglass atop a pedestal, flanked by a hand holding a mirror on the left and a hand holding a serpent on the right, with hills and trees in the background. The verse initials Q and C are decorative enlarged letters. The title's first word is set in large capitals with a possible decorative upright form of "T" in "TEMPORE". The line "Quisquis es" reads as printed. Line-end spacing in the verse is uneven, which may be a setting feature rather than a fault.
